selectedChecks.result: Label supports alkaline inactivation and lists the three comparator diluents used in the question.
Label supports avoiding calcium admixtures because of precipitation. The question asks for the incompatible solution rather than inferring a universal calcium diluent.
Label supports interpreting unbound exposure when albumin/renal/hepatic factors change.
Label and algorithm support transient AV block, methylxanthine antagonism, dipyridamole potentiation, rapid delivery/flush, and relevant respiratory cautions.
Label supports the indication-specific 0.9 mg/kg, maximum 90 mg, initial 10% and remainder over 60 minutes; stroke guideline scope may extend beyond the label window in selected patients.

Additional questions remain within the taught entries: losartan selected additional uses, lithium/RAAS review and AT1 effects; paracetamol fever/liver-risk/NSAID distinction; ibuprofen exposure and CV precautions; cefazolin product-specific preparation and incision-level rationale; tramadol monoamine pathways, named CNS depressants and nausea; meropenem indication, product/order verification and CNS risk; promethazine H1 action, postural BP and route verification. Current primary labels were consulted for the selected pharmacological and safety claims. The tramadol reference is extended release: no release-specific instruction, numerical dose, or route conversion was transferred to the ward capsule. Ward brand/stock observations remain content provenance, not proof of current availability. This is a partial author review, not independent clinical approval or exhaustive coverage.
